description: Everything the shell is allowed to do. Deliberately almost nothing: the window renders the frontend and the frontend talks to the backend over HTTP. `dialog:allow-open` is the folder picker for choosing a workspace (§16.2) - it can only open a chooser, and the path it returns is validated on the backend like any other untrusted input. The shell plugin is registered for Rust only: no permission here lets the page execute anything. The updater's three permissions are the whole of what an in-place update needs - ask, fetch, install - and what it fetches is verified against the public key in tauri.conf.json before anything is written, so this grants the page a way to install an update from whoever holds the private key and no way to install anything else. `process:allow-restart` is what brings the new copy up afterwards; `allow-exit` is deliberately not here, so the page can restart the app and cannot quit it.
